userStories.title: Override publishing for one CLI or chat run
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] `resolvePublishCliOverride(undefined)` returns `undefined`.
[unit] `resolvePublishCliOverride("none")` returns `{ workflow: { publish: "none" } }`.
[unit] `resolvePublishCliOverride("push")` returns `{ workflow: { publish: "push" } }`.
[unit] `resolvePublishCliOverride("draft")` returns `{ error: 'nax run --publish must be one of pr, push, none (got "draft")' }`.
[unit] `resolvePublishCliOverride("")` returns an `error` result naming `(got "")`.

[unit] `loadConfig` with project `workflow: { publish: "pr", maxFixRounds: 3 }` and CLI overrides `{ workflow: { publish: "none" } }` resolves `workflow.publish` to `"none"`, preserving `workflow.maxFixRounds: 3`.
[unit] `resolveRunProjectContext(workdir, { feature: "f1", publish: "none" })` returns `cliOverrides.workflow` equal to `{ publish: "none" }`.
[unit] `resolveRunProjectContext(workdir, { feature: "f1" })` returns `cliOverrides` with no `workflow` key.
[cli] `nax run -f f1 --publish draft`, spawned in a temporary project directory, exits with code 1 and prints `nax run --publish must be one of pr, push, none (got "draft")` on stderr.
[unit] `parseJobInput("run", { feature: "f1", profiles: [], publish: "none" })` returns `{ kind: "run", feature: "f1", profiles: [], publish: "none" }`.
[unit] `parseJobInput("run", { feature: "f1", profiles: [], publish: "draft" })` returns `{ error: '[chat] publish must be one of "pr", "push", "none"' }`.
[unit] `parseJobInput("run", { feature: "f1", profiles: [] })` returns an input with no `publish` key.
[unit] `buildJobArgv({ kind: "run", feature: "f1", profiles: [], maxCost: 5, publish: "none" }, ctx)` returns an argv whose last four tokens are `--max-cost`, `5`, `--publish`, `none`.
[unit] `buildJobArgv({ kind: "run", feature: "f1", profiles: [] }, ctx)` returns an argv with no `--publish` token.
[unit] `buildChainStepArgv` of `parseChainStepInput("run", { feature: "f1", publish: "none" })` returns an argv whose last two tokens are `--publish`, `none`.
[unit] The `nax-jobs__run` tool's input schema declares a `publish` property whose `enum` is `["pr", "push", "none"]`.
[unit] `resolveRunProjectContext(workdir, { feature: "f1", publishOnly: true, publish: "push" })` returns `cliOverrides.workflow` equal to `{ publish: "push" }`.

routing.reasoning: Each touchpoint forwards one optional enum through existing config and argv paths; a single-session mapper, merge, and subprocess test is sufficient without changing publish execution.

modifiedFiles.reason: the `CHAIN_STEP_FIELDS` expectation pins `run` to `["feature", "profiles", "maxCost", "repo"]`; the run step gains the `publish` field, so it expects `["feature", "profiles", "maxCost", "repo", "publish"]` and every other key is unchanged.

userStories.title: Read and bound the transferable workflow record
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] `readHandoffRecordFiles(dir)` over one run `r1` holding `result.json` and `ledger.md` returns `ok: true`, `newestRunId: "r1"` and the entries `{ runId: "r1", file: "result.json" }` then `{ runId: "r1", file: "ledger.md" }`.
[unit] Each entry's `content` equals the file's UTF-8 text.
[unit] Each entry's `mtimeMs` equals `Math.trunc` of the file's stat mtime.
[unit] With runs `r1` (older `result.json` mtime) and `r2` (newer), the entries list `r2`'s files before `r1`'s and `newestRunId` is `"r2"`.
[unit] A run directory holding `result.json` but no `ledger.md` contributes one `result.json` entry and the result is `ok: true`.
[unit] A run directory with no `result.json` contributes no entry and does not count toward the run limit.
[unit] An empty workflow dir returns `{ ok: false, reason: "no finished workflow run for this feature; run nax run first" }`.
[unit] A workflow dir that does not exist returns the same `no finished workflow run for this feature; run nax run first` reason.
[unit] 21 run directories that each hold a `result.json` return `ok: false` with reason `the feature has 21 workflow runs; koda accepts at most 20`.
[unit] 20 such run directories return `ok: true`.
[unit] Two runs whose `result.json` mtimes are equal and largest return `ok: false` with reason `two workflow runs share the newest result.json time, so the newest run is ambiguous`.

[unit] Two runs whose newest `result.json` mtimes are `1000.2` and `1000.7` ms return the same `two workflow runs share the newest result.json time, so the newest run is ambiguous` reason, because both truncate to `1000`.
[unit] A record whose contents total 524289 UTF-8 bytes returns `ok: false` with reason `the run record is 524289 bytes; koda accepts at most 524288`.
[unit] A record whose contents total exactly 524288 UTF-8 bytes, with a 2-byte character counted as 2, returns `ok: true`.
[unit] A run whose `ledger.md` holds a NUL character returns `ok: false` with reason `ledger.md of run <runId> holds a NUL or unpaired surrogate character, which koda refuses`.
[unit] `isStorableRecordText("a\u0000b")` returns false.
[unit] `isStorableRecordText` of a string holding the lone surrogate `\uD800` returns false; a file cannot produce one through UTF-8 decoding, so this case is pinned on the helper.
[unit] `isStorableRecordText` of a string holding a valid surrogate pair (an emoji) returns true.

routing.reasoning: Contained filesystem reader using ordinary stat, encoding and limit checks, with no cross-process integration in this story.

userStories.title: Validate the newest finished record and committed PRD
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] `collectHandoffRecord` over one run whose feature record is `step: "done"`, `outcome: "local-only"`, `head: "<H>"`, with `_handoffRecordDeps.git` answering a `prd.json` whose `branchName` is the branch and every story passed, returns `ok: true` with the entries `readHandoffRecordFiles` returns.
[unit] `collectHandoffRecord` calls `_handoffRecordDeps.git` with `["show", "<H>:.nax/features/f1/prd.json"]` and the repo root.
[unit] A `readHandoffRecordFiles` refusal (an empty workflow dir) is returned unchanged and `_handoffRecordDeps.git` is not called.
[unit] A newest `result.json` that is not JSON returns `ok: false` with reason `the newest workflow run's result.json is not a finished feature record`.
[unit] A newest `result.json` with `schemaVersion: 2` returns `ok: false` with reason `the newest workflow run's result.json is not a finished feature record`.
[unit] A newest `result.json` with `schemaVersion: 1` and no `featureWorkflow` returns `ok: false` with reason `the newest workflow run's result.json is not a finished feature record`.
[unit] A newest done feature record with no `outcome` returns `ok: false` with reason `the newest workflow run's result.json is not a finished feature record`.
[unit] A newest feature record with `step: "publish"` returns `ok: false` with reason `the workflow stopped at publish; run nax run to finish it`.

[unit] A newest feature record with `outcome: "draft"` and `url: "https://x/pull/7"` returns `ok: false` with reason `the run already published a draft PR https://x/pull/7; a handoff needs a run that ended without a PR (publish "none")`.

[unit] A newest feature record with `outcome: "ready"` and no `url` returns `ok: false` with reason `the run already published a ready PR; a handoff needs a run that ended without a PR (publish "none")`.

[unit] Given a schema-version-1 newest record with `step: "done"`, a matching committed PRD with no pending stories, and `outcome: "pushed"` with `head` equal to `input.head`, `collectHandoffRecord` returns `ok: true`.
[unit] A newest feature record whose `head` differs from `input.head` returns `ok: false` with reason `HEAD moved since the workflow finished; run nax run so the new commits are reviewed`.
[unit] `_handoffRecordDeps.git` answering a non-zero exit returns `ok: false` with reason `prd.json is not committed at HEAD`.
[unit] A `prd.json` at HEAD whose text is the JSON array `[]` returns `ok: false` with reason `prd.json at HEAD is not a PRD`.
[unit] A `prd.json` at HEAD whose `userStories` holds a `null` entry returns `ok: false` with reason `prd.json at HEAD is not a PRD`.
[unit] A `prd.json` at HEAD whose `branchName` is `feat/other` while `input.branch` is `feat/f1` returns `ok: false` with reason `prd.json names branch feat/other, not feat/f1`.
[unit] A `prd.json` at HEAD with stories `US-002` and `US-003` pending returns `ok: false` with reason `2 stories are still pending: US-002, US-003`.
[unit] A `prd.json` at HEAD with only `US-002` pending returns `ok: false` with reason `1 story is still pending: US-002`.

routing.reasoning: Adds ordered validation to one existing collector using the established Git stub seam, so real run fixtures and stubbed Git replies cover it without an integration session.

userStories.title: Refuse a second local publisher for a marked run
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] `writeHandoffMark(runDir, { schemaVersion: 1, at: "2026-11-18T00:00:00.000Z", flowId: "fl1", url: "https://koda/flows/fl1" })` writes `<runDir>/handoff.json`, and parsing it returns the same object.
[unit] `writeHandoffMark` leaves the mtime of `<runDir>/result.json` unchanged.
[unit] `readNewestHandoffMark(dir)` returns `{ mark, path }` with `path` equal to `<newest run dir>/handoff.json` when the run with the newest `result.json` mtime holds a mark.
[unit] `readNewestHandoffMark(dir)` returns `null` when only an older run holds a mark and the newest run has none.
[unit] `readNewestHandoffMark(dir)` returns `null` when the newest run's `handoff.json` is not JSON.
[unit] `readNewestHandoffMark(dir)` returns `null` for a workflow dir that does not exist.

[unit] `handoffMarkRefusal("f1", { mark: { schemaVersion: 1, at: "T", flowId: "fl1", url: "https://koda/flows/fl1" }, path: "/r/handoff.json" })` returns `f1 was handed off to koda (flow fl1 https://koda/flows/fl1) at T; koda publishes it. Delete /r/handoff.json to publish it here instead`.
[unit] `handoffMarkRefusal` for a mark with `requestId: "rq1"` and no `flowId` names `(approval request rq1)` in place of the flow.

[unit] `runWorkflowFeature` with `publishOnly: true` on a feature whose newest run holds a mark, and whose newest record would otherwise resume publishing, throws `NaxError` code `WORKFLOW_PUBLISH_ONLY_REFUSED` with a message beginning `[workflow] --publish-only: f1 was handed off to koda`, and no publish step runs.

[unit] The chat publish launch (`nax-jobs__publish` tool `run`) for a feature with every story passed, with `_jobsLaunchDeps.readNewestHandoffMark` stubbed to return a mark, returns an error result whose content begins `[chat] f1 was handed off to koda`, and requests no approval card.

[unit] With every story passed, `readNewestHandoffMark` stubbed to return `null`, and no prior publication at HEAD, `nax-jobs__publish` runs the existing published-at-head check and requests the normal publish card, unchanged.
[unit] The chat publish launch on a feature with pending stories returns the existing pending-stories refusal and does not call `readNewestHandoffMark`.
[unit] `handoffMarkRefusal` for a mark with `outcomeUnknown: true` and neither `flowId` nor `requestId` names `(outcome unknown; check koda's flows first)`.

[unit] A chat publish launch refused by a handoff mark, while an active chain's next step is a publish of the same feature in the same repo, stops that chain with the refusal text without its `[chat] ` prefix.

routing.reasoning: A local duplicate-publish safeguard, not an authentication or access-control change: temporary files and the two existing refusal seams cover the standard IO and guard paths.

routing.reasoning: The parser, schema, and prompt change is local; reviewer and supervisor are model identifiers whose syntax is checked, not user roles or permissions.

the assertion that `FLOW_SEND_INPUT_SCHEMA.required` equals `["features", "roles", "costCapUsd"]`; `features` is no longer required by the schema because the handoff form omits it, so it expects `["roles", "costCapUsd"]`, and spec-form send behaviour is unchanged.

userStories.title: Send a finished feature to koda and mark the local run
userStories.description:
**Goal** — After local preflight and direct user approval, push exactly the reviewed commit, send the handoff body, and mark the run according to koda's answer.

**Motivation** — The owner therefore ruled (koda design `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-17-flow-handoff-design.md`, APPROVED 2026-11-17): **hand over before publishing**, and **upload the run record with the handoff request**, because `.nax/features/<feature>/workflow/` is git-excluded and exists only on the machine that ran the chain.

**Approach** — The tool's `run` routes before any parse: a body with `handoff` and no `features` (`Object.hasOwn`) goes to the handoff send; every other body goes to `parseFlowSendInput` and today's spec-form send, which refuses both-or-neither.

The handoff send, in a new module `packages/nax/src/chat/flow/flow-handoff.ts`, runs in this order (outside a chain in this story):

1. Parse. Errors return the existing `[chat] the flow request is invalid:` list.
2. `readFlowRepoState(repoRoot, [])` (branch, clean tree with untracked files counted, head sha, normalised remote), then `checkFlowBranch(branch, [])`.
3. `collectHandoffRecord({ repoRoot, feature, head: state.sha, branch: state.branch })`; a refusal returns `[chat] cannot hand off <feature>: <reason>`.
4. `readNewestHandoffMark`; a found mark returns `[chat] ` + `handoffMarkRefusal(...)`.
5. Approval: a direct call shows one card. The card's summary is `hand <feature> over to koda`, its command is `git push --set-upstream origin <branch>`, and its reason lists the repository line, `feature <feature>: <N> run(s), <B> bytes of run record` (N is the number of distinct run ids, B the UTF-8 byte total), the roles, the cost cap and the billing note.
6. On allow: the spec form's post-allow sequence, which now returns `PostAllowResult = { readonly result: ToolResult; readonly created?: FlowCreateOutcome; readonly unknown?: true }` (`created` set on a 201 or 202 answer, `unknown` set when the push happened and koda's answer was lost or unusable: error codes `MEMORY_KODA_TIMEOUT`, `MEMORY_KODA_UNREACHABLE`, `MEMORY_KODA_ABORTED`, `FLOW_KODA_UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE`, `MEMORY_KODA_BAD_RESPONSE`); the spec form uses only `result`. It runs (re-check that HEAD and tree are unchanged, push target, push destination, `commitAndPush` with `skipCommit`, create), with an empty spec-path list for the push-target re-read and the handoff body below. Preserve sourceSha pinning, verified remote, cancellation and existing tool-result text. Explicit koda HTTP refusal leaves the branch pushed without writing a mark. Cancellation or branch movement before push also writes no mark.
7. On a created or held answer: `writeHandoffMark(<newest run dir>, { schemaVersion: 1, at, flowId, url } | { schemaVersion: 1, at, requestId })`, then the result text. When `unknown` is set (the branch is pushed and koda may have the flow): `writeHandoffMark(<newest run dir>, { schemaVersion: 1, at, outcomeUnknown: true })`, then the existing spec-form message. A mark write failure does not change the result; it appends `; the local handoff mark could not be written (<message>), so nothing stops a local publish of <feature>`. Use the collected `newestRunId` for the mark, the existing joined flow URL for a 201, and the injected clock for the ISO timestamp.

Every collaborator of the handoff send is behind an exported `_flowHandoffDeps = { collectHandoffRecord, readNewestHandoffMark, writeHandoffMark, now }` in `flow-handoff.ts`, re-exported from `chat/flow/index.ts`; the push, repo reads and koda create stay on `_flowProviderDeps`.

`createKodaFlow`'s `body` parameter widens to `FlowCreateBody | FlowHandoffCreateBody`; its 201/202 handling is unchanged. `flow-provider.ts` is at 540 lines of the 600-line cap, so the handoff path lives in `flow-handoff.ts` and the spec-form helpers it reuses (card text escaping, push destination, the post-allow sequence, koda failure messages) move out of `flow-provider.ts` into a new `flow-send-steps.ts` that both import. To keep one stub target without an import cycle, the `_flowProviderDeps` object moves to a new leaf module `flow-deps.ts` that `flow-provider.ts`, `flow-send-steps.ts` and `flow-handoff.ts` all import; `flow-provider.ts` re-exports that same object, so every existing `_flowProviderDeps` stub in `flow-provider.test.ts`, `flow-provider-cancel.test.ts` and `chat-host-jobs.test.ts` still replaces what the moved helpers call. The moved push-target re-check takes the spec paths as a parameter instead of reading them from a `FlowSendInput`. The constants the moved code uses move with it into `flow-send-steps.ts`: `FLOW_PUSH_COMMIT_MESSAGE`, `BILLING_NOTE`, `TOOL_NAME`, and the declined, cancelled, branch-changed and push-target-moved messages. `flow-provider.ts` imports them from there and re-exports `FLOW_PUSH_COMMIT_MESSAGE`, which `chat/flow/index.ts` and the tests import. No value import runs from `flow-send-steps.ts` or `flow-deps.ts` back to `flow-provider.ts`, so `check:import-cycles` gains no module. Chat imports the workflow helpers by relative path, with no change to the workflow barrel.

**Scope** — In: direct send, preflight, approval, pinned push, shared helpers, koda create and local mark. Out: chain admission/lifecycle and controller wiring (US-008); GitLab remotes; tracked-files-only tree checks; sending any additional workflow file or changing koda, its runner or the wire contract.

**Interface** — Body sent to koda (the contract in koda `.nax/features/flow-handoff/spec.md` § Wire shape):
```ts
export interface FlowHandoffCreateBody {
  readonly remoteUrl: string;
  readonly branch: string;
  readonly roles: FlowSendRoles;
  readonly costCapUsd: number;
  readonly handoff: { readonly feature: string; readonly headSha: string; readonly record: readonly HandoffRecordFile[] };
}
```
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] The `nax-flow__send` tool's `run` with a handoff body, with `_flowHandoffDeps.collectHandoffRecord` stubbed to return `{ ok: false, reason: "R" }`, returns the error result `[chat] cannot hand off f1: R`, requests no approval, pushes nothing and calls no koda create.
[unit] The tool's `run` with a handoff body calls `collectHandoffRecord` with `{ repoRoot, feature: "f1", head, branch }` taken from `readFlowRepoState(repoRoot, [])`.

[unit] With the record accepted and `_flowHandoffDeps.readNewestHandoffMark` returning a mark, the tool returns an error result beginning `[chat] f1 was handed off to koda`, requests no approval and pushes nothing.
[unit] With no active chain the tool requests one approval card whose `summary` is `hand f1 over to koda`.
[unit] That card's `command` is `git push --set-upstream origin <branch>` and its `reason` contains `feature f1: 2 run(s)` for a record of two run ids.
[unit] On a denied card the tool returns the existing declined result and pushes nothing.
[unit] On an allowed card the tool calls `commitAndPush` with `skipCommit: true` and `sourceSha` equal to the carded sha.

[unit] On an allowed card `createKodaFlow` receives `{ remoteUrl, branch, roles, costCapUsd, handoff: { feature: "f1", headSha, record } }` with the collected record and no `features` or `specSha` key.

[unit] A 201 answer `{ id: "fl1", state: "PENDING", url: "/flows/fl1" }` (stubbed at `createKodaFlow` as the `kind: "created"` outcome) makes the tool call `writeHandoffMark` on the collected newest run dir with `flowId: "fl1"` and the joined flow URL, and return a success result whose first line is the JSON `{ flow: "fl1", state: "PENDING", url }` using the joined URL.
[unit] A 202 answer (stubbed as `{ kind: "held", requestId: "rq1" }` at `createKodaFlow`) makes the tool write a mark with `requestId: "rq1"` and return the existing held result text.

[unit] A koda HTTP 409 answer (`createKodaFlow` rejects with `MEMORY_KODA_HTTP`, `context.status: 409`, and koda message `duplicate`) returns the existing `[chat] koda did not create the flow (HTTP 409): duplicate; branch <branch> stays pushed` result and `writeHandoffMark` is not called.

[unit] `createKodaFlow` rejecting with `NaxError` code `MEMORY_KODA_TIMEOUT` after the push makes the tool write a mark with `outcomeUnknown: true` and return the existing `koda could not be reached` result.

[unit] `createKodaFlow` rejecting with `NaxError` code `FLOW_KODA_UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE` makes the tool write a mark with `outcomeUnknown: true` and return the existing `koda answered unexpectedly` result.
[unit] The turn cancelled during the create (`MEMORY_KODA_ABORTED`) makes the tool write a mark with `outcomeUnknown: true`, preserving the existing cancelled-during-request message.
[unit] The turn cancelled after the card and before the push returns the existing `the turn was cancelled; nothing was pushed` result and `writeHandoffMark` is not called.
[unit] The branch moved between the card and the push returns the existing `the branch changed while the card was open; nothing was pushed` result and calls no koda create or mark writer.

[unit] `writeHandoffMark` rejecting with `EACCES` after a 201 answer leaves the result a success whose text ends `; the local handoff mark could not be written (EACCES), so nothing stops a local publish of f1`.

[unit] Given an allowed card for a valid spec-form body (`features`, no `handoff`), `createKodaFlow` receives the existing spec body with `features` and `specSha`, and the tool never calls `collectHandoffRecord`.
[unit] `createKodaFlow` rejecting with `MEMORY_KODA_UNREACHABLE` after the push causes an `outcomeUnknown: true` mark, preserving the existing `koda could not be reached` result.
[unit] `createKodaFlow` rejecting with `MEMORY_KODA_BAD_RESPONSE` after the push causes an `outcomeUnknown: true` mark, preserving the existing `koda answered unexpectedly` result.

routing.reasoning: The bundle reuses the existing push and create architecture but changes their shared approval-gated path; isolate tests for authorized external writes and post-push outcome classification.

userStories.title: Approve handoff only as the last step of a valid chain
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] `resolveChainProposal` for steps `[run f1 with publish "none", handoff f1 with roles and costCapUsd 5]` with `handoffAvailable: true` returns two steps, the second with `kind: "handoff"`, `target: "f1"` and `argv` equal to `handoffStepArgv` of its input.
[unit] `resolveChainProposal` with a handoff step whose `feature` is `"../x"` returns an error beginning `[chat] step 2:` that names `handoff.feature`.
[unit] `resolveChainProposal` with a handoff step carrying a `repo` field returns an error naming that field as unknown.
[unit] `resolveChainProposal` with a handoff step and `handoffAvailable` unset returns `[chat] step 1: handoff needs a koda connection (memory.koda in the nax config)`.
[unit] With `handoffAvailable: true`, `resolveChainProposal` for `[handoff f1, run f2]` returns `[chat] step 1: a handoff must be the chain's last step`.

[unit] With `handoffAvailable: true`, `resolveChainProposal` for `[run f1 without publish, handoff f1]` returns `[chat] step 2: step 1 runs f1 without publish "none", so it would publish its own PR before the handoff`.

[unit] With `handoffAvailable: true`, `resolveChainProposal` for `[run f1 with publish "push", handoff f1]` returns `[chat] step 2: step 1 runs f1 without publish "none", so it would publish its own PR before the handoff`.
[unit] With `handoffAvailable: true`, `resolveChainProposal` for `[publish f1, handoff f1]` returns `[chat] step 2: step 1 publishes f1, so there would be nothing to hand off`.

[unit] With `handoffAvailable: true`, `resolveChainProposal` for `[run f1 with publish "none" in a repo resolving to another root, handoff f1]` returns `[chat] step 2: the handoff runs in <chat root>, but step 1 runs f1 in <other root>` with both resolved paths.
[unit] With `handoffAvailable: true`, `resolveChainProposal` for `[run f2 without publish, handoff f1]` returns two steps: a run of another feature is not subject to handoff restrictions.

[unit] With `handoffAvailable: true`, the `nax-jobs__chain` card for `[run f1 with publish "none", handoff f1 with reviewer r, supervisor s and costCapUsd 5]` has the step line `2. hand f1 to koda (reviewer r, supervisor s, cost cap $5.00) — starts after: step 1 succeeded`.
[unit] The same card has the line `koda asks for its own approval before anything billed starts`.

routing.reasoning: Adds a chain-only step with repo-aware constraints and a card that authorizes the external send's reviewer, supervisor and cost cap.

modifiedFiles.reason: the `CHAIN_STEP_FIELDS` expectation lists the job kinds only; the chain gains a `handoff` step kind, so it also expects `handoff: ["feature", "roles", "costCapUsd"]`.

suggestedCriteria: [unit] With `handoffAvailable` unset, `resolveChainProposal` still accepts a valid run-only chain and returns its existing run argv unchanged.

userStories.title: Run an approved handoff without a second card and settle the chain
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Use the existing chain approval for an exact final handoff call and record its success or failure without a synthetic process job.

**Motivation** — The 2026-11-04 ruling splits the work: koda owns the always-on flow, including the finish (rulings, then ready); a chat chain is the tool for one feature watched in one sitting.

**Approach** — Inside an approved chain the handoff step runs without a second card, like every other chain step. A direct `nax-flow__send` handoff call outside a chain keeps its card. koda's own approval still gates anything billed.

Approval: when `chains.admit({ kind: "handoff", argv: handoffStepArgv(input) })` answers `auto`, no card is shown; otherwise the card is shown, carrying the admission's `note` when there is one. When the send was auto-admitted, `chains.stepEnded(chainId, step, "succeeded" | "failed", note)` reports the outcome: `succeeded` for a created or held answer, `failed` with the result text for every other outcome after admission, the outcome-unknown answers included.

A refusal at steps 1 to 4, while `chains.active()` has a next step of kind `handoff` whose target is this feature, stops that chain with the refusal text without its `[chat] ` prefix, the same rule `stopRefusedPublishStep` applies to a publish. The four pre-admission stages are parsing, repo/branch validation, record collection, and newest-mark validation. After an auto admission, `stepEnded` is called exactly once in a `finally`, so a thrown error ends the step `failed` with `flow send failed: <message>`. Mark write failure on a created or held outcome does not change the step to failed.

`ChatChains` gains `stepEnded(chainId: string, step: number, state: "succeeded" | "failed", note: string): void`. `ChainStep` gains `ended?: { state; note; at }`, and `ChainSummary.steps[]` carries it. A `succeeded` end on the last step marks the chain `completed`; a `failed` end stops it with `step <n> handoff failed: <note>`; a call for a chain that is not current or a step that is not the admitted one is ignored. `admit` treats a handoff exactly as a job launch: kind and argv must match the next step, and the previous step's job must have succeeded. Use the existing chain clock and audit persistence for the step terminal event. `ChainLaunch.kind` widens to `ChainStepKind`; `ChainSummary.steps[].kind` already uses it after US-007.

`createFlowProvider`'s options gain `chains?: ChatChains`, and `createHostJobs` (`packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/jobs-host.ts`) passes its controller. `createHostJobs` sets `handoffAvailable` true exactly when `kodaFlowConnection(config)` is defined. `hostProviders` passes the same controller to the flow provider. Preserve direct approval for spec sends and for unadmitted handoff calls.

`buildJobsInstructions` keeps its line count. Its eleventh line (index 10, `workflow-builder.ts:249`) becomes exactly: While a chain is active, call each step's launch tool with exactly the approved arguments, one step at a time, after the previous step succeeded; a different call stops the chain and shows a normal card. A handoff step's launch tool is `nax-flow__send` with `handoff: { feature }` and exactly the approved roles and cost cap. Update `workflow-builder-chain.test.ts` with this line only (the other pinned lines and line count stay unchanged); update the jobs host options expectation and add `stepEnded: mock(() => {})` to the typed fake in `jobs-launch-chain.test.ts`, retaining all prior expectations.

**Scope** — In: controller type and transition changes, pre-admission stop, exactly-once admitted end, host and jobs prompt wiring. Out: direct send mechanics (US-006), proposal validation (US-007), charging koda's flow cap against the chain cap, or changing koda's separate approval.

**Interface**
```ts
stepEnded(chainId: string, step: number, state: "succeeded" | "failed", note: string): void;
```
`ChainStep.ended` and `ChainSummary.steps[].ended` carry state, note and timestamp; `FlowProviderOptions` gains `chains?: ChatChains`.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] `admit({ kind: "handoff", argv })` on an active chain whose step 1 run job succeeded and whose step 2 is that handoff returns `{ kind: "auto", step: 2 }`.
[unit] `admit({ kind: "handoff", argv })` with a different cost cap token stops the chain with `off-card step` and returns a card admission.
[unit] `admit({ kind: "handoff", argv })` while step 1's run job is still running stops the chain with `step 1 has not succeeded`.
[unit] `stepEnded(chainId, 2, "succeeded", "flow fl1")` on the last step marks the chain `completed`, and `summary().steps[1].ended.state` is `"succeeded"`.
[unit] `stepEnded(chainId, 2, "failed", "X")` stops the chain with reason `step 2 handoff failed: X`.
[unit] `stepEnded` for a chain id that is not current, or for a step other than the admitted one, leaves the chain state and its steps unchanged.

[integration] Through `createHostJobs` with a koda connection and an approved chain `[run f1 with publish "none", handoff f1]` whose run job succeeded, the `nax-flow__send` handoff call with exactly the approved roles and cost cap requests no approval card, creates the flow (stub `createKodaFlow` with the `kind: "created"` outcome for HTTP 201), and leaves the chain `completed`.

[integration] The same path with an HTTP 409 refusal (`createKodaFlow` rejects with `MEMORY_KODA_HTTP` and `context.status: 409`) leaves the chain `stopped` with a reason beginning `step 2 handoff failed: [chat] koda did not create the flow (HTTP 409)`.
[integration] The same path with `_flowHandoffDeps.collectHandoffRecord` refusing with reason `R` leaves the chain `stopped` with reason `cannot hand off f1: R`, and requests no card.

[unit] A `nax-flow__send` handoff call while no chain is active never calls `stepEnded` or `stop`.
[unit] `createHostJobs` with a config that has no koda connection passes `handoffAvailable: false` to the jobs provider, and with a koda connection passes `true`.

[unit] An auto-admitted handoff whose create outcome is unknown after the push ends `failed` with the existing result text, preserving the outcome-unknown mark.
[unit] An auto-admitted handoff cancelled or refused for a moved branch before push ends `failed`, preserving the existing `nothing was pushed` result and absence of a mark.
[unit] An auto-admitted handoff whose mark write fails after a created or held answer ends `succeeded`, preserving the success result with the appended mark warning.

analysis:
Goal and delivery: Close #2968 (items 6 and 7, the nax half of koda #477; the receiving half merged in koda PR #478). The operator approves a chat chain, its run finishes without publishing, and the final handoff pushes the reviewed commit and sends the git-excluded run record to koda. koda publishes under its own identity and owns REVIEW, RULE and FIX; a held create is a successful transfer for nax, not yet an existing flow or a waiver of koda billing approval. The blocker is identity, not PR visibility: packages/nax/src/workflow/item-thread-state.ts:65 reads the index through ownComments(comments, login) at :70, and packages/nax/src/bot/workflow-ready.ts:46 rejects a missing index. This is an enhancement to the existing Bun/TypeScript nax package only. The codebase-memory MCP tools were not exposed here; structural findings were verified with repository reads and text search. Binding story ownership follows the Stories and Acceptance Criteria sections, not the shorthand story references in the Design prose.

US-001: packages/nax/bin/nax.ts:266 registers publish-only and :289 calls resolveRunProjectContext before loadConfig. Validate the new flag at the start of the run action, before bakeoff/schedule/project work, not at the loader or after the trust and plan gates. packages/nax/bin/run-action.ts:282 builds profile and context overrides using the mapper at packages/nax/src/cli/run-context-overrides.ts:44; packages/nax/src/config/loader.ts:168 deep-merges the CLI block and calls it at :283. The existing mode type/default and local-only finish are at packages/nax/src/config/runtime-types-workflow.ts:37, packages/nax/src/config/schemas-workflow.ts:57 and packages/nax/src/workflow/finalize.ts:574; no new finalizer or config schema is required. packages/nax/src/cli/publish-only-refusal.ts:17 is a separate flag/pending-story guard. packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/job-argv.ts:72 and :152 feed both the launch path (packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/jobs-launch.ts:442) and chain token building (packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/chain-argv.ts:11 and :35). Add only the run-tool schema field at packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/jobs-provider.ts; ordinary jobs and omitted arguments must keep byte-for-byte argv behavior. Use existing run-action, run-context override, workflow-config, job-argv, chain-argv and jobs-provider tests; copy the isolated Bun.spawn pattern at packages/nax/test/unit/cli/trust.test.ts:270, capturing stderr independently.

US-002 and US-003: packages/nax/src/workflow/result.ts:127 supplies result-file mtime ordering and skips missing results, covered at packages/nax/test/unit/workflow/result.test.ts:83. Its comparison uses floats; handoff tie/newest decisions must use the integer wire values (float ordering may still distinguish older tied groups). Do not change existing result consumers. packages/nax/src/workflow/result.ts:39 additionally checks the stories member, so the handoff validator should check the transferred text against the stated contract, not accidentally inherit that reader's additional shape or pick an older good record. packages/nax/src/workflow/paths.ts:10 builds the workflow path, packages/nax/src/config/paths/index.ts:158 owns feature paths, and packages/nax/src/workflow/config-change.ts:132 demonstrates git show at a commit through a mutable seam. packages/nax/src/workflow/publish-only.ts:61 is the resume reference, not a substitute for handoff validation: it tolerates outcomes that handoff must reject, orders HEAD differently, and feeds other callers. packages/nax/src/prd/index.ts:268 supplies pending ids in PRD order; it is not equivalent to a new all-stories-passed filter for every terminal status. Check raw PRD structure before calling it, and read from the reviewed commit, not the working tree. Test shape failures on temp workflow dirs and semantic checks with a stubbed git result; preserve first-failure precedence and avoid invoking git on a record refusal.

US-004: packages/nax/src/workflow/feature-context.ts:106 confirms fc.featureDir is the workflow directory. packages/nax/src/workflow/feature.ts:228 ensures the ledger and consults publishOnlyStart at :237; a new directory with only a ledger does not change the newest result. Guard only publish-only before that decision. packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/jobs-launch.ts:320 prioritizes pending stories, :292 matches a refused publish against the feature and resolved repo root, and :398 stops a matching waiting chain; set the existing publishedAtHead routing flag without changing the older published/transient-draft behavior. Tests extend packages/nax/test/unit/workflow/feature.test.ts:429 and packages/nax/test/unit/chat/jobs/jobs-launch.test.ts:326 and jobs-launch-chain.test.ts:278 in the same directory. The sidecar is not a tracked lock or a schema change. A fresh result supersedes it; an unreadable/malformed mark or a failed write cannot prevent publication, and deletion is an explicit operator override, not proof that koda did not receive the handoff.

US-005 and US-006: packages/nax/src/chat/flow/flow-input.ts:178 and :188 validate model strings and :198 validates the cap; keep one implementation, ordered spec errors and current spec defaults. packages/nax/src/chat/flow/flow-provider.ts:112 is the advertised schema, :165 is the mutable test seam, :452 is the post-approval sequence and :504 is outer tool handling. Extract shared helpers and dependency object without adding a reverse value import; packages/nax/src/chat/flow/index.ts:29 and existing suites import the current re-exports. packages/nax/src/chat/flow/flow-repo.ts:220 and :251 verify a publishable branch, fully clean tree, HEAD, GitHub identity and branch rules; an empty spec list is deliberate. The shared path currently re-reads both branch/origin and the actual push destination, passes a pinned source SHA and verified destination and uses the turn signal. Preserve the distinction between the normalized repository sent to koda and the transport URL passed only to git. packages/nax/src/chat/flow/flow-koda.ts:125 already models 201 and 202; use the same client and connection. packages/nax/src/memory/koda-http.ts:370 recognizes explicit MEMORY_KODA_HTTP errors only: an unexpected response with a status in its context is still an unknown handoff outcome, not an explicit HTTP refusal. Do not retry or roll back a pushed branch on an ambiguous create; write the conservative local mark and surface any write failure without converting the original outcome. Regression coverage includes packages/nax/test/unit/chat/flow/flow-input.test.ts, flow-provider.test.ts:154 and :427, flow-provider-cancel.test.ts, flow-repo.test.ts:424, flow-koda.test.ts, plus packages/nax/test/unit/chat/chat-host-jobs.test.ts and packages/nax/test/unit/prompts/builders/flow-builder.test.ts. Stub shared external collaborators by mutating the original exported object so both send forms observe the same replacement.

US-007 and US-008: packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/chain-tools.ts:35 parses job inputs, :54 resolves their repos, :109 validates the proposal and :141/:171 produce the card. Add handoff as a chain-only kind; do not broaden the process-job parser/runner. Validate earlier same-feature steps using the resolved root, not the raw repo field or a coincidental argv value. Guard callsites such as isRunJobKind in chainReason when widening the union (packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/job-types.ts:57). packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/chain-controller.ts:104 reconciles terminal jobs and holds, :177 admits by exact argv, and :279 feeds job status via packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/jobs-provider.ts:102. The final handoff is not a spawned job: its terminal event must be recorded and persisted through the existing serialized audit writer, not inferred from the preceding job. Avoid reopening stopped chains or applying stale/duplicate ends to a different admission. Retain held-draft, prior-success, cost-cap, session-change and close behavior for job steps. packages/nax/src/chat/jobs/jobs-host.ts:29 installs the flow provider only with kodaFlowConnection and bypasses the jobs full-mode approval wrapper for external sends; :53 creates the single controller, and :71 constructs the jobs provider. Derive availability from the same connection and share the controller, while retaining the direct flow card outside an approved exact handoff. Relevant coverage: packages/nax/test/unit/chat/jobs/chain-argv.test.ts:46, chain-tools-repo.test.ts, chain-tool-card.test.ts, chain-controller.test.ts, chain-transitions.test.ts, jobs-host.test.ts:56, jobs-launch-chain.test.ts and packages/nax/test/unit/prompts/builders/workflow-builder-chain.test.ts:122.

Compatibility and rollout: No config, PRD, workflow result or audit-record migration, no dependency additions, and no changes to another workspace or koda. Old flags, spec sends, existing job chains and records without marks remain usable; the schema's only intended input-error change for old malformed spec requests is the both-or-neither message. Build the independent stories US-001/002/004/005 first, then US-003 and US-007, then US-006 (after US-003/004/005), finally US-008. Enable via the existing koda connection, use a clean GitHub checkout with the finished PRD committed at HEAD, and opt in with a run's publish: none and last-step handoff. Existing drafts must be finished under the publisher's identity; they are not adopted. Worktree and record snapshots are separate and the mark is best-effort, so this is not a distributed transaction or a guarantee against unrelated processes racing a local publish. For approval safety, keep the rechecks, payload allowlist and exact chain admission; for support after an unknown result, check koda before retrying or removing the mark. Use Bun unit tests mirroring source, keep the source and test size constraints (split tests by describe above 650 lines), keep workflow barrel unchanged, and avoid new cycles (packages/nax/package.json:15/:21).
outOfScope: Adopting a draft PR already published from chat: the owner chose hand-over-before-publish (koda design approach A).
GitLab remotes for the handoff form: `readFlowRepoState` accepts GitHub remotes only, as the spec form does today.
Refusing a plain `nax run` (not `--publish-only`) or a chat `run` launch on a handed-off feature: the design lets a fresh run write a newer record, which leaves the mark on an older run.
Clearing or listing handoff marks with a command: the refusal names the file to delete.
Changing koda, its runner, or the wire contract in koda `.nax/features/flow-handoff/spec.md`.
Counting the koda flow's `costCapUsd` against the chain's own `costCap`.
A tracked-files-only tree check for the handoff: the handoff reuses `readFlowRepoState`, which also refuses untracked files, as the spec form does.
Sending `package-branch*.diff`, `branch-review.json` or any workflow file other than `result.json` and `ledger.md`.
Updating koda's design doc status or nax's slice-2 design doc: done by hand after the run.
